# #[wildcard] on a component says which names in its package's namespace
# resolve to it — a package whose member set cannot be enumerated says so once
# instead of every unknown name being either an error or silently accepted.
#
# This is a txtar rather than a fixture because a wildcard is consulted through
# an imported package's namespace, and the checker's testdata harness resolves
# directory imports through a stub.

sngl check app.sngl
stdout 'ok'

# A declared name beats the wildcard: box() is box, not the wildcard.
sngl check declared.sngl
stdout 'ok'

# The wildcard widens which names resolve; it does not stop their props being
# checked. An undeclared prop on a wildcard-resolved component is still one.
! sngl check badprop.sngl
stderr 'unknown prop "nope" on component element'

# A name no wildcard covers is still unknown.
! sngl check nomatch.sngl
stderr 'unknown component "Widget" in package w'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:app"
import "./widgets"

component main() {
    window {
        widgets.marquee(tag = "marquee")
        widgets.blink(tag = "blink")
    }
}

-- declared.sngl --
import . "sngl:app"
import "./widgets"

component main() {
    window {
        widgets.box(label = "declared")
    }
}

-- badprop.sngl --
import . "sngl:app"
import "./widgets"

component main() {
    window {
        widgets.marquee(tag = "marquee", nope = 1)
    }
}

-- nomatch.sngl --
import . "sngl:app"
import w "./widgets"

component main() {
    window {
        w.Widget(tag = "x")
    }
}

-- widgets/widgets.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:macro"

#[wildcard("[a-z][a-z0-9]*")]
component element(tag string) {
    text(value = tag)
}

component box(label string) {
    text(value = label)
}
